hero.title: Your skin barrier's favorite engineer
hero.sentence: Sofia Panting studies chemical engineering at Purdue and reads the ingredient label so you don't have to.

paragraphs: I didn't become obsessed with skincare because my skin was perfect. I became obsessed when nothing seemed to work anymore.
Growing up in Honduras I never thought much about my skin. Then I moved to the U.S., and the routine that had always worked for me stopped working.

Acne, hair that changed with the water, and a lot of products that promised everything. Studying chemical engineering gave me a way to sort through it: read the label, understand the molecule, then decide.
This journal is where I write that down. The science behind the products, my real routine, and what earns a permanent spot on my shelf.

decoder.title: Decode a label
decoder.sentence: Paste the ingredient list from the back of any product. I'll tell you what each ingredient is there to do.

about.letter:
Hi, I'm Sofia.

I'm a chemical engineering student at Purdue, originally from Honduras, and I've spent the last few years learning why some formulas work and most of the marketing doesn't.

Every post here starts the same way: with the ingredient list. I look at what each molecule does, how much of it is likely in there, and whether the claim on the front of the bottle holds up.

I'm not here to sell you a ten-step routine. I want you to understand what you're putting on your face, so you can shop with confidence and skip the hype.
